etymology_story.zh: underclothe 由 underclothing“内衣”逆构而来，即把词尾 -ing 去掉，形成表示“提供内衣”的动词；其中 clothe 可追溯至古英语。[词源依据](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/underclothe)
etymology_story.en: Underclothe was back-formed from underclothing by removing what looks like the ending -ing, producing a verb meaning to provide underwear; clothe ultimately goes back to Old English. [Etymological source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/underclothe)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 under-（在里面、在下面）+ clothe（给……穿衣），但历史形成方式是逆构。屈折形式：underclothes、underclothed、underclothing；相关词族：clothe（给……穿衣）、clothes（衣服）、clothing（衣物）、underclothes／underclothing（内衣）。underclothed 也可表示“穿得太少的”，须按语境区分。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, under- meaning beneath combines with clothe, although the historical formation was back-formation. Inflections: underclothes, underclothed, underclothing. Related family: clothe, clothes, clothing, underclothes, and underclothing. Underclothed can also mean insufficiently dressed, so context matters.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: provide with underwear（提供内衣）是最清楚的现代释义；clothe（供给衣服、给……穿衣）范围更广；dress（给……穿衣）侧重穿衣动作。后两者不专指内衣。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Provide with underwear is the clearest modern equivalent; clothe covers clothing generally; dress emphasizes putting clothes on someone. The latter two do not specifically refer to underwear.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: under“里面”+ clothe“给穿衣”：把贴身那一层配齐。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Under + clothe: supply the layer worn underneath.

etymology_story.zh: 鱼名由 cod“鳕鱼”加表示幼小者的 -ling 构成；苹果名则来自中古英语 querdlyng 的变形，更早来源尚不确定，两者不能统一解释为“鳕鱼的幼小者”。[词源依据](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/codling)
etymology_story.en: The fish name combines cod with the diminutive suffix -ling; the apple name developed from Middle English querdlyng, whose earlier origin is uncertain, and has a separate history. [Etymological source](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/codling)

morphology_enriched.zh: 鱼义：cod（鳕鱼）+ -ling（幼小者）；苹果义在现代英语中宜作为整体词记忆。鱼义复数为 codling 或 codlings，苹果义通常为 codlings；苹果名另有拼写 codlin。相关复合词 codling moth 指“苹果蠹蛾”，其中 codling 与苹果有关；没有常用的派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Fish sense: cod + diminutive -ling; the apple sense is best treated as a whole word in modern English. Fish plurals are codling or codlings; the apple plural is normally codlings. Codlin is an alternative spelling of the apple name. In codling moth, codling refers to apples. There are no common derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: young cod（幼鳕）准确对应幼鱼义；hake（无须鳕）仅对应某些鱼类俗名用法；cooking apple（烹调用苹果）是苹果义的上位词，范围比 codling 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Young cod precisely matches the juvenile-fish sense; hake corresponds only to certain fish-name uses; cooking apple is a broader term covering the culinary apple sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鱼义记 cod + -ling＝小鳕鱼；苹果义另开一格，苹果蠹蛾帮助联想。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For fish, cod + -ling means little cod; keep the apple meaning separate, linked to codling moth.

senses.meaning_zh: 一般公认为安全的，指食品物质的特定预期用途获得合格专家普遍认可为安全
senses.meaning_en: generally recognized as safe by qualified experts under specified conditions of intended use
senses.english_definition: If a food substance's intended use is GRAS, qualified experts generally recognize that use as safe under the specified conditions.
senses.collocation_en: GRAS status; GRAS determination
senses.collocation_zh: 一般公认为安全的地位；一般公认为安全的认定

senses.sentence_zh: 专家组认定，该配料在其预期用途条件下可被一般公认为安全。

etymology_story.zh: GRAS 取自 Generally Recognized As Safe 的首字母，成为美国食品监管中的专门缩略语；这一概念与 1958 年《食品添加剂修正案》确立的制度有关，安全认定针对特定使用条件。[美国食品药品监督管理局释义](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-ingredients-packaging/generally-recognized-safe-gras)
etymology_story.en: GRAS takes the initial letters of Generally Recognized As Safe and became a technical abbreviation in US food regulation associated with the framework established by the 1958 Food Additives Amendment; the safety assessment concerns specified conditions of use. [FDA explanation](https://www.fda.gov/food/food-ingredients-packaging/generally-recognized-safe-gras)

morphology_enriched.zh: Generally（一般地、普遍地）+ Recognized（被认可）+ As（为）+ Safe（安全的）→ GRAS；属于首字母缩略构词，不是词根加词缀。形式通常不变，无常用屈折或派生词；常见术语有 GRAS status（GRAS 地位）、GRAS determination（GRAS 认定）、GRAS notice（GRAS 通报）。
morphology_enriched.en: Generally + Recognized + As + Safe → GRAS: an acronym formed from initials, rather than a root-and-affix construction. It is normally invariant and has no common inflections or derivatives. Established combinations include GRAS status, GRAS determination, and GRAS notice.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: generally recognized as safe（一般公认为安全）是完整展开形式；safe for the intended use（在预期用途下安全）是近义描述，但未表达专家普遍认可这一条件；FDA-approved（经 FDA 批准的）不是同义词，表示不同的监管情况。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Generally recognized as safe is the full expansion; safe for the intended use is a near-equivalent description that omits general expert recognition; FDA-approved is not a synonym and describes a different regulatory situation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: G-R-A-S：普遍认可为安全；记住“谁认可”和“什么用途”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: G-R-A-S: generally recognized as safe—remember who recognizes safety and for which use.

senses.meaning_en: decorative work made by fitting together thin pieces of wood or other materials to form patterns
senses.english_definition: Marquetry is the craft or decoration in which thin pieces of wood or other materials are fitted together to make patterns on furniture or other surfaces.
senses.collocation_en: floral marquetry; marquetry panels
senses.collocation_zh: 花卉图案拼镶细工；拼镶装饰板

senses.sentence_zh: 柜门上饰有精致的花卉图案拼镶细工。

etymology_story.zh: 借自中古法语 marqueterie，源于 marqueter“做成方格花纹、镶嵌”，进一步关联 marque“标记”；词义由制作装饰性花纹发展为这种工艺及其成品装饰。[词源依据](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/marquetry)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Middle French marqueterie, it derives from marqueter meaning to checker or inlay, ultimately related to marque meaning mark; it denotes both the decorative craft and its resulting decoration. [Etymological source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/marquetry)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 marquetry 作为整体借词处理，不强拆为独立词根和生产性后缀。另有较少见拼写 marqueterie；通常作不可数名词，无常用派生词。marquetry-like（像拼镶细工的）是可临时构成的形容词；marquetry maker（拼镶细工匠）是描述性短语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, marquetry is best treated as a whole borrowed word rather than forced into a productive root-and-suffix analysis. Marqueterie is a less common spelling. It is normally uncountable and has no common derivatives. Marquetry-like is a possible descriptive adjective, and marquetry maker is a descriptive phrase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inlay（镶嵌装饰）范围更广，通常指把材料嵌入基底的凹槽；parquetry（几何木片拼花）强调几何图案，常用于地板；intarsia（嵌木细工）与 marquetry 意义交叠，但也用于其他工艺领域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inlay is broader and typically involves setting material into a recessed base; parquetry emphasizes geometric wood patterns, often in flooring; intarsia overlaps with marquetry but also has meanings in other crafts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“做花纹”联想到：薄木片像拼图一样拼成装饰画。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 par force 借自盎格鲁法语，原义为“凭借力量、强行”；后来由外在强力引申为情势所迫，成为现代正式用语中的“不得不、必然地”。[词源依据](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/perforce)
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed Anglo-French par force, originally meaning through force or physical compulsion; the meaning later extended to necessity imposed by circumstances, producing its modern formal sense. [Etymological source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/perforce)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是固定副词，可借历史结构 par／per（凭借）+ force（力量）理解，但不是现代仍有生产性的前缀构词。无屈折变化或常用直接派生词；force（力量、强迫）、forceful（强有力的）、forcible（使用强力的）、forcibly（强行地）属于相关 force 词族，并非由 perforce 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: It is a fixed modern adverb, understandable through historical par/per meaning by plus force, rather than a currently productive prefix construction. It has no inflections or common direct derivatives. Force, forceful, forcible, and forcibly belong to the related force family, rather than deriving from perforce.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: necessarily（必然地）可表达逻辑或事实上的必要性；unavoidably（不可避免地）强调无法避开；inevitably（必然地、终究）强调结果必将发生。perforce 尤其突出情势使人别无选择，语体更正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Necessarily can express logical or factual necessity; unavoidably emphasizes the impossibility of avoiding something; inevitably stresses an outcome that is certain to occur. Perforce particularly suggests that circumstances leave no alternative and is more formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 情势的 force“力量”推着走，所以“不得不”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The force of circumstances pushes you along: you have no choice.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经葡萄牙语 piranha 借入这个南美鱼名，源头是图皮语中表示“鱼”和“牙齿”的成分。其锋利牙齿和捕食形象又促成了形容凶狠掠夺者的比喻用法。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/piranha)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed piranha through Portuguese from a Tupi name combining elements meaning 'fish' and 'tooth.' The fish's sharp teeth and predatory image also motivated figurative references to aggressively acquisitive people. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/piranha)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，piranha 是不可再按英语词缀规则拆分的借入名词；图皮语的“鱼＋牙齿”属于历史词源分析。屈折变化：piranha → piranhas，也可用 piranha 作复数；可自由构成 piranha-like（像水虎鱼的），但这不是固定的核心派生词。没有常用的同根动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, piranha is an unanalyzed borrowed noun; the Tupi 'fish + tooth' analysis belongs to its historical origin. Inflection: piranha → piranhas, with unchanged piranha also used as a plural. Piranha-like is a transparent, freely formed compound rather than an established core derivative. There is no common corresponding verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: caribe（水虎鱼的地区性别称）最接近同义词；predator（捕食者）是范围更广的上位词；shark（鲨鱼；比喻坑骗或掠夺他人者）只在比喻义上部分接近，不能替代鱼类名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Caribe is a regional alternative name for a piranha; predator is a broader category rather than an exact synonym; shark overlaps figuratively when describing someone who exploits others, but denotes a different fish literally.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史命名逻辑：“鱼＋牙齿”——先记尖牙鱼，再联想凶狠的掠夺者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical naming hook: 'fish + tooth'—picture a sharp-toothed fish, then extend that image to a ruthless predator.

etymology_story.zh: turgid 于17世纪初由拉丁语 turgidus（膨胀的）进入英语，后者来自 turgēre（鼓起、膨胀）。后来，“身体鼓胀”的形象被用于语言，形成“言辞膨胀、文风浮夸”的比喻义。[词源依据：在线词源词典](https://www.etymonline.com/word/turgid)
etymology_story.en: Turgid entered English in the early seventeenth century from Latin turgidus, 'swollen,' derived from turgēre, 'to swell.' Physical swelling later supplied a metaphor for inflated, overelaborate language. [Etymological source: Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/turgid)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代常用分析以 turgid 为完整形容词词基，不把 turg 当作可独立使用的英语词。派生：turgid + -ly → turgidly（浮夸地；肿胀地）；turgid + -ity → turgidity（膨胀；言辞浮夸）；turgid + -ness → turgidness（膨胀；浮夸）。历史同根词包括 turgor（膨压）、turgescent（正在膨胀的）和 turgescence／turgescency（膨胀状态），它们不是由 turgid 直接派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: For ordinary modern analysis, turgid is the complete adjective base; turg is not an independent English word. Derivatives: turgid + -ly → turgidly; turgid + -ity → turgidity; turgid + -ness → turgidness. Historical relatives include turgor, turgescent, and turgescence/turgescency; these are related formations, not direct derivatives of turgid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: swollen（肿胀的）是最普通的物理状态用词；distended（胀大的）强调从内部撑大；bombastic（言辞浮夸的）强调炫耀性的宏大措辞，而 turgid 还常暗示冗赘、难懂和乏味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Swollen is the general everyday term for physical enlargement; distended emphasizes expansion from within; bombastic stresses showily grand language, whereas turgid often also suggests density, difficulty, and dullness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“胀”：细胞胀满水，文章胀满大词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the idea of swelling: cells swell with water; prose swells with elaborate words.

etymology_story.zh: uncouth 源自古英语 uncūth，即 un-（不）与 cūth（已知的、熟悉的）的组合，最初表示“未知的、陌生的”。词义后来由“陌生、古怪”发展为“不文雅、粗野”；现代诙谐用法中的 couth（文雅的）受到 uncouth 的反向影响。[词源依据：牛津高阶学习词典](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/uncouth)
etymology_story.en: Uncouth comes from Old English uncūth, combining un-, 'not,' with cūth, 'known or familiar,' and originally meant 'unknown or unfamiliar.' Its meaning developed through strangeness toward lack of refinement; modern humorous couth, meaning 'cultured,' was influenced by its interpretation as the opposite of uncouth. [Etymological source: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/uncouth)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可联想为 un-（不）＋ couth（文雅的）→ uncouth，但这一分析需要结合历史理解：古英语 cūth 表示“已知的”，并非现代“文雅的”。派生：uncouth + -ly → uncouthly（粗野地）；uncouth + -ness → uncouthness（粗俗、无礼）。相关词有 couth（文雅的，通常带诙谐色彩）及较少见的 couthness（文雅、教养）。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern mnemonic analysis is un-, 'not,' + couth, 'cultured,' but historically cūth meant 'known,' not 'cultured.' Derivatives: uncouth + -ly → uncouthly; uncouth + -ness → uncouthness. Related forms include humorous couth and the less common noun couthness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rude（无礼的）侧重冒犯他人或违反礼貌；boorish（粗鄙的）侧重缺乏教养和体谅；coarse（粗俗的）常用于低俗的言语或举止。uncouth 综合强调举止不文雅、不符合社交规范。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rude emphasizes discourtesy or offence; boorish suggests poor manners and little consideration for others; coarse often describes vulgar speech or behaviour. Uncouth broadly emphasizes a conspicuous lack of social refinement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史线索：“不熟悉”→“古怪”→“不合礼数”；现代用 couth“文雅”与 uncouth“粗野”成对记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical path: unfamiliar → strange → socially unpolished; then pair modern couth, 'cultured,' with uncouth.

etymology_story.zh: wayfaring 可追溯至古英语 wegfarende，由 weg（道路）与 faran（行进）的现在分词组成，原指“在路上行进的”。中古英语形式后来受到 -ing 词尾的影响，逐渐形成现代拼写，并保留尤指徒步行旅的文学色彩。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/wayfaring)
etymology_story.en: Wayfaring descends from Old English wegfarende, combining weg, 'way,' with the present participle of faran, 'to travel.' Its Middle English form was reshaped under the influence of -ing, producing the modern form with its literary association with travelling, especially on foot. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/wayfaring)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构：way（道路）＋ fare（行进）＋ -ing → wayfaring，其中 fare 加 -ing 时去掉末尾不发音的 e。词族：wayfare（行旅，罕见动词）、wayfares、wayfared；wayfarer（旅人，尤指徒步旅人）、wayfarers。wayfaring 的形容词用法和名词用法仍可见于文学语境，但不应据此把罕见动词 wayfare 标为常用词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: way + fare, 'travel,' + -ing → wayfaring, with the silent final e of fare dropped. The family includes the rare verb wayfare, its forms wayfares and wayfared, and the noun wayfarer, plural wayfarers. Adjectival and nominal wayfaring remain available in literary contexts; the related rare verb does not justify presenting a common verb use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: travelling（旅行中的；旅行）最中性，不限定方式；wandering（漫游中的；漫游）强调路线或目的地不固定；itinerant（巡回的、辗转各地的）常指因工作而不断迁移。wayfaring 带文学色彩，常让人想到沿路徒步前行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Travelling is neutral and does not specify a mode of transport; wandering suggests no fixed route or destination; itinerant often describes repeated movement connected with work. Wayfaring is literary and commonly evokes a person proceeding along a road on foot.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: way 是路，fare 在这里是行进：沿路前行，就是 wayfaring。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Way is the road; fare here means travel: travelling along the road gives you wayfaring.

etymology_story.zh: aperitif 借自法语 apéritif；法语中相应的形容词曾表示具有通利或开胃作用，最终可追溯到拉丁语 aperīre（打开）。这个名称后来用于餐前饮用、旨在增进食欲的酒。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/aperitif)
etymology_story.en: Aperitif was borrowed from French apéritif, whose corresponding adjective referred to an opening or appetite-stimulating effect and ultimately derives from Latin aperīre, 'to open.' The noun came to denote a drink taken before a meal to encourage the appetite. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/aperitif)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 aperitif 作为整体借入名词使用，不宜机械拆成英语词根与后缀。屈折变化：aperitif + -s → aperitifs；apéritif 是保留法语重音符号的拼写变体。没有常用的英语动词、副词或固定形容词派生；aperture（孔、开口）和 aperient（通便的；通便药）属于历史同根词，不是由 aperitif 派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats aperitif as a whole borrowed noun, rather than a productive combination of English roots and suffixes. Inflection: aperitif + -s → aperitifs; apéritif is the spelling retaining the French accent. There is no common derived English verb, adverb, or established adjective. Aperture and aperient are historical relatives, not derivatives of aperitif.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pre-dinner drink（餐前饮品）范围更广，不一定具有开胃用途；cocktail（鸡尾酒）指混合调制的酒，可作为开胃酒，也可在其他时候饮用；digestif（餐后助消化酒）是对照词，通常在餐后饮用，不能与 aperitif 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pre-dinner drink is broader and need not imply an appetite-stimulating purpose; cocktail denotes a mixed drink that may or may not serve as an aperitif; digestif is a contrasting term for an alcoholic drink taken after a meal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“打开”→餐前“打开胃口”的一杯酒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin 'open' → a drink that 'opens' your appetite before dinner.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自荷兰语 burger，意思是“城镇市民”，其中 burg 指设防的城镇，与德语 Bürger 同源。它由城镇公民的身份发展出“富足而体面的市民”义；在斯里兰卡，首字母大写的 Burgher 又成为特定族群的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Dutch burger, meaning a town citizen, from burg, a fortified town; German Bürger is a cognate. It developed an additional sense of a prosperous, respectable townsman, while capitalized Burgher became the name of a particular community in Sri Lanka.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可按 burgh（城镇）+ -er（居民或相关的人）理解，但全词历史上是借词。常见形式：burgher、复数 burghers；相关词 burgh、borough 都含有古老的“设防城镇”概念，并非由 burgher 派生。表示斯里兰卡族群的 Burgher 可作名词和形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: A transparent modern analysis is burgh (town) + -er (inhabitant or associated person), although the complete word was historically borrowed. Common forms are burgher and plural burghers; related burgh and borough share the older fortified-town concept but are not derivatives of burgher. Capitalized Burgher functions as both a noun and an adjective for the Sri Lankan community.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: townsman 指男性城镇居民，强调居住地；citizen 强调公民身份或权利；bourgeois 强调中产阶级身份及价值观，常带批评意味。burgher 尤其适合历史城镇语境，也可略带调侃地描写富足、守成的市民；这些词不能替代族群名称 Burgher。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Townsman identifies a male town resident; citizen emphasizes civic membership or rights; bourgeois emphasizes middle-class status and values, often critically. Burgher is especially suited to historical towns and can suggest prosperous conventionality with a mildly humorous tone; these alternatives do not replace the ethnic name Burgher.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: burgh“城镇”+ -er“人”：先记“城里有市民身份的人”，再联想到富足、体面的老城居民。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Burgh means town and -er suggests a person: picture a recognized town citizen, then a prosperous, respectable resident.

etymology_story.zh: 形容词 chippy 由 chip 与 -y 构成，其“好争吵”义通常与 have a chip on one's shoulder 这一表示心怀不平、随时准备争执的习语联系起来。两个非正式名词分别与炸薯条 chips 和木匠工作时产生的木屑 chips 有关。
etymology_story.en: The adjective combines chip with -y, and its quarrelsome meaning is usually linked with having a chip on one's shoulder. The informal nouns refer respectively to the chips sold in a fish-and-chip shop and the wood chips associated with a carpenter's work.

morphology_enriched.zh: 形容词：chip + -y → chippy；比较级 chippier，最高级 chippiest，副词 chippily，名词 chippiness。名词的复数为 chippies，另有拼写 chippie；相关基础词族包括 chip、chips、chipped、chipping。
morphology_enriched.en: Adjective: chip + -y → chippy; comparative chippier, superlative chippiest, adverb chippily, and noun chippiness. The noun plural is chippies, and chippie is an alternative spelling; the underlying word family includes chip, chips, chipped, and chipping.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词近义词：touchy 强调敏感、容易被冒犯；irritable 强调容易烦躁；combative 强调主动争辩或对抗。chippy 常把敏感与挑衅结合起来；名词义分别对应 fish-and-chip shop“炸鱼薯条店”和 carpenter“木匠”，但语体更口语化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adjective, touchy stresses sensitivity to offence, irritable stresses a tendency to become annoyed, and combative stresses readiness to confront others. Chippy often combines sensitivity with provocation; its noun equivalents are fish-and-chip shop and carpenter, both less colloquial.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect three chips: a chip on the shoulder suggests argument, chips on a plate suggest the shop, and wood chips suggest the carpenter.

etymology_story.en: Jerkin was recorded in English in the early sixteenth century for a close-fitting short jacket; its earlier origin is uncertain. It is often used of historical clothing and was also applied to certain sleeveless leather military or work garments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 jerkin 作为不可进一步可靠拆解的词干，不宜分析为 jerk + -in。常见屈折形式为 jerkin、复数 jerkins；没有常用的派生动词或形容词，jerkin-like 只是可临时组成的“像这种短上衣的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, jerkin is best treated as an unanalyzed stem, rather than jerk + -in. Its common inflectional forms are jerkin and plural jerkins; it has no common derived verb or adjective, although jerkin-like can be formed descriptively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: waistcoat 指通常穿在衬衫外的无袖背心；doublet 指欧洲历史上的贴身短上衣，通常有袖；jacket 是夹克、短外套的泛称。jerkin 特别突出历史服装色彩，且通常无袖、常为皮制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A waistcoat is a sleeveless garment usually worn over a shirt; a doublet is a close-fitting historical European jacket, usually with sleeves; jacket is the broad general term. Jerkin particularly suggests historical dress and is usually sleeveless and often leather.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Fix one image in memory: a historical figure wearing a fitted, sleeveless leather jacket over a shirt.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自土耳其语 paşa，是奥斯曼帝国授予高级军政官员的尊衔，通常置于姓名之后；其更早来源存在争议。英语后来借这种权贵形象，比喻生活奢适、惯于受人伺候的人。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Turkish paşa, an Ottoman title for senior military and civil officials, normally placed after a person's name; its earlier origin is disputed. English later extended it figuratively to a man accustomed to luxury and personal service.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 pasha 作为完整借词词干；复数为 pashas。历史词族包括 pashalik 或 pashalic“帕夏管辖的地区或职位”，以及较罕见的 pashadom“帕夏的地位、统治或领地”；这些相关词如今主要见于历史语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats pasha as a complete borrowed stem; its plural is pashas. Historical derivatives include pashalik or pashalic, a pasha's jurisdiction or office, and the rarer pashadom, a pasha's status, rule, or territory; these related forms occur chiefly in historical contexts.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: governor 指地方行政长官，只对应部分帕夏的职务；dignitary 泛指身居高位的要人；potentate 强调强大的统治权。pasha 是特定历史制度中的尊衔，不能与这些词完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Governor names an administrative role held by some pashas; dignitary broadly means a person of high rank; potentate emphasizes ruling power. Pasha is a title belonging to a particular historical system, so these words are only approximate equivalents.

meaning: 机敏有力的反驳；迅速回击

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 riposte 进入英语，源自意大利语 risposta“回答”，与 rispondere“回答、回应”有关。它先用于击剑中挡开进攻后的还击，随后引申为言语上迅速而有力的反驳。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French riposte, from Italian risposta, meaning an answer, related to rispondere, to answer or respond. Its fencing sense of an attack following a parry developed into the figurative sense of a quick, effective verbal reply.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 riposte 视为完整借词词干，不宜机械拆成英语前后缀。名词复数与动词第三人称单数均为 ripostes；过去式、过去分词为 riposted，现在分词为 riposting，后者须去掉词尾不发音的 e。response、respond 与它在词源上相关，但不是由 riposte 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats riposte as a complete borrowed stem rather than a combination of productive English affixes. Ripostes is both the noun plural and the third-person singular verb; riposted is the past tense and past participle, and riposting drops the final silent e. Response and respond are etymologically related, not derivatives of riposte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: retort 强调迅速而尖锐的反驳，可能带怒气；rejoinder 较正式，强调针对前话的回答；comeback 较口语化，强调巧妙回嘴。riposte 尤其突出回击的敏捷、机智和效果，在击剑中另有明确的技术含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Retort suggests a quick, sharp reply, sometimes angry; rejoinder is more formal and emphasizes an answering response; comeback is informal and often highlights a clever reply. Riposte particularly suggests speed, wit, and effectiveness, and it also has a precise technical meaning in fencing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先挡住，再刺回去：剑上是防守还击，话里是机智反驳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Block, then strike back: with a sword it is a fencing counterattack; with words it is a clever reply.

etymology_story.zh: bedlam 源于伦敦圣玛丽伯利恒医院名称的通俗变体，Bethlem 和 Bedlem 都与 Bethlehem 有关。这个名称后来由精神病院的旧称引申为喧闹混乱的场面，这种引申反映了历史上的社会观念。
etymology_story.en: Bedlam developed from a popular form of the name of London's Hospital of St. Mary of Bethlehem, with Bethlem and Bedlem representing forms of Bethlehem. Its extension from an old name for a psychiatric hospital to noisy disorder reflects historical social attitudes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bedlam 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的整体词，不能分析为 bed（床）+ lam。词族包括 bedlamite（历史用词，曾指精神病院病人或被认为精神失常的人；如今用于称呼人有冒犯性）及其复数 bedlamites；表示喧闹混乱的 bedlam 通常不可数，没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bedlam is a simple lexical base, not a combination of bed and lam. Its family includes bedlamite, a historical term for a psychiatric hospital patient or someone considered mentally ill, now offensive when applied to people, and its plural bedlamites; bedlam meaning noisy disorder is normally uncountable and has no common derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chaos（混乱）强调缺乏秩序，不一定有噪声；uproar（喧嚣、骚动）强调响亮的叫喊或强烈的公众反应；pandemonium（大混乱）与 bedlam 接近，也强调喧闹失控，语气通常更强烈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chaos emphasizes a lack of order without necessarily involving noise; uproar emphasizes loud shouting or a strong public reaction; pandemonium closely resembles bedlam but often sounds more dramatic and intense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住演变链：Bethlehem 医院名 → Bedlam 旧称 → 喧闹混乱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical chain: Bethlehem hospital name → Bedlam → noisy confusion.

etymology_story.zh: disinherited 是 disinherit 的过去式和过去分词；disinherit 在中古英语后期由表示剥夺的 dis- 与 inherit 构成，取代了更早、与古法语 desheriter 有关的 disherit。其意义由剥夺家产继承权扩展为剥夺一个人或群体应有的权利与共同遗产。
etymology_story.en: Disinherited is the past tense and past participle of disinherit, formed in late Middle English from privative dis- and inherit, replacing the earlier disherit associated with Old French desheriter. The meaning broadened from exclusion from a family inheritance to deprivation of rights or a shared heritage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 [dis-（剥夺、取消）+ inherit（继承）] + -ed（过去式、过去分词或分词形容词标记）；由于 inherit 以 /t/ 结尾，-ed 读 /ɪd/。主要词族包括 inherit（继承）、inherits、inherited、inheriting、inheritance（继承；遗产）、inheritor（继承人）、inheritable（可继承的）、inheritability（可继承性），以及 disinherit（剥夺继承权）、disinherits、disinheriting、disinherited 和 disinheritance（继承权的剥夺）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is [dis- meaning removal or deprivation + inherit] + -ed, marking the past tense, past participle, or a participial adjective; -ed is pronounced /ɪd/ because inherit ends in /t/. The main family comprises inherit, inherits, inherited, inheriting, inheritance, inheritor, inheritable, inheritability, disinherit, disinherits, disinheriting, disinherited, and disinheritance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dispossessed（被剥夺财产或土地的）强调失去占有物；disowned（被断绝关系或不被承认的）强调亲属或社会关系遭到否认，不一定涉及遗产；disadvantaged（处于不利地位的）对应社会引申义，但不一定表示有人主动剥夺其权益。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dispossessed emphasizes the loss of property or land; disowned emphasizes rejection of a family or social relationship without necessarily involving inheritance; disadvantaged matches the broader social sense but does not necessarily imply deliberate deprivation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: inherit 是继承，dis- 把资格拿走，-ed 表示已经发生或形成的状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inherit means receive an inheritance; dis- removes that entitlement, and -ed marks the completed action or resulting state.

etymology_story.zh: footplate 是英语 foot（脚）与 plate（板）的复合词，十九世纪中叶已见使用，字面意思就是脚下站立的板。它尤其用于机车驾驶室的平台，也用于其他机器的站立操作平台。
etymology_story.en: Footplate is a compound of foot and plate, recorded by the mid-nineteenth century, literally describing a plate beneath the feet. It became particularly associated with the working platform of a locomotive and also denotes standing platforms on other machinery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 foot（脚）+ plate（板）→ footplate；复数为 footplates，不能把内部的 foot 改为 feet。相关复合词包括 footplateman（机车驾驶乘务人员，主要为英国铁路用语；复数 footplatemen）；footplate crew（机车驾驶乘务组）和 footplate worker（机车驾驶工作人员）中的 footplate 是名词作定语，并非独立的形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is foot + plate → footplate, with the plural footplates; the internal element foot does not become feet. Related compounds include footplateman, chiefly a British railway term for a locomotive crew member, with plural footplatemen; in footplate crew and footplate worker, footplate is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: platform（平台）含义更广，不限于脚下操作区域；footboard（踏脚板）可供踩踏或支脚，但通常不特指机车驾驶操作平台；cab floor（驾驶室地板）描述整个驾驶室的地面，未必强调乘务人员站立操作的区域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Platform is broader and need not refer to a standing area at machinery; footboard can support the feet or provide a step but is not the usual precise term for a locomotive's working platform; cab floor describes the cab's flooring without specifically emphasizing the crew's operating position.

etymology_story.zh: hypotensive 是二十世纪初出现的医学构词，与 hypotension（低血压）相联系，由希腊语来源的 hypo-（低于）和拉丁语来源、表示张力或压力的词干结合而成。它既可以表示血压过低的状态，也可以表示使血压下降的作用，并进一步用作相关药物或患者的名词。
etymology_story.en: Hypotensive emerged in early twentieth-century medical vocabulary in association with hypotension, combining Greek-derived hypo-, meaning below, with a Latin-derived stem connected with tension or pressure. It describes either low blood pressure or an effect that lowers it, and also functions as a noun for a relevant agent or person.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 hypo-（低于正常）+ tens-（张力、压力）+ -ive（具有某种性质或作用的），也可联系 hypotension → hypotensive 的名词—形容词对应。主要词族包括 hypotension（低血压）、hypotensive（低血压的；降压的；降压药；低血压者）和 hypotensively（以低血压或降压的方式，较少用）；对照词族包括 hypertension（高血压）、hypertensive（高血压的；高血压者）、normotension（正常血压）、normotensive（血压正常的；血压正常者）和 antihypertensive（抗高血压的；抗高血压药）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure can be analyzed as hypo- meaning below normal + tens- meaning tension or pressure + -ive indicating a property or effect, alongside the noun–adjective correspondence hypotension → hypotensive. The main family includes hypotension, hypotensive, and the less frequent adverb hypotensively; contrasting formations include hypertension, hypertensive, normotension, normotensive, and antihypertensive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: low-blood-pressure（低血压的）是状态义的通俗表达，通常放在名词前；blood-pressure-lowering（降低血压的）明确表达降压作用，不表示患者本身血压过低；antihypertensive（抗高血压的；抗高血压药）强调治疗高血压，而 hypotensive 的降压作用也可能是非预期效应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Low-blood-pressure is a plain-language, usually attributive equivalent for the condition; blood-pressure-lowering explicitly describes an effect rather than a patient's existing condition; antihypertensive emphasizes treatment of high blood pressure, whereas a hypotensive effect may also be unintended.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hypo- 是低，tens- 是压力：压力已经低，或被药物降下来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hypo- means low and tens- suggests pressure: pressure is low, or something lowers it.

etymology_story.zh: mitotic 来自 mitosis（有丝分裂）；mitosis 是十九世纪经德语形成的科学术语，其核心来源是希腊语 mitos，意为线或经线。命名着眼于分裂细胞中可观察到的线状染色体结构。
etymology_story.en: Mitotic derives from mitosis, a nineteenth-century scientific term formed through German from Greek mitos, meaning thread or warp thread. The name refers to the threadlike chromosome structures visible in dividing cells.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式为 mitot-（mitosis 对应的构词词干）+ -ic（与……有关的）→ mitotic，不能机械地写成 mitosis + -ic。主要词族包括 mitosis（有丝分裂；复数 mitoses）、mitotic（有丝分裂的）、mitotically（通过有丝分裂地）、antimitotic（抗有丝分裂的；抗有丝分裂药）、amitosis（无丝分裂）、amitotic（无丝分裂的）、endomitosis（核内有丝分裂）和 endomitotic（核内有丝分裂的）；mitogen（促有丝分裂原）与 mitogenic（促有丝分裂的）是相关的同源构词。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is mitot-, the combining stem corresponding to mitosis, + -ic meaning relating to → mitotic, rather than mechanically adding -ic to the unchanged word mitosis. The main family includes mitosis, plural mitoses, mitotic, mitotically, antimitotic, amitosis, amitotic, endomitosis, and endomitotic; mitogen and mitogenic are related formations sharing the underlying root.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: karyokinetic（核分裂的）侧重细胞核的分裂过程，在部分专业语境中与 mitotic 接近；cell-dividing（细胞分裂的）含义更宽，不限定有丝分裂机制；proliferative（增殖的）强调细胞数量增加，也可指组织的增殖状态，不能直接替换 mitotic spindle 中的 mitotic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Karyokinetic focuses on nuclear division and overlaps with mitotic in some technical contexts; cell-dividing is broader and does not specify mitosis; proliferative emphasizes an increase in cell numbers or a tissue's growth activity and cannot directly replace mitotic in mitotic spindle.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mitos＝线：看到线状染色体参与分裂，就联想到 mitotic。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mitos means thread: picture threadlike chromosomes being separated during mitosis.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 obversus，意为“转向……的”，由 ob-（朝向）与 vertere（转）构成；“朝向观察者的一面”发展为钱币的“正面”，后来又引申为相互对应的“相反面”。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/obverse)
etymology_story.en: Obverse comes from Latin obversus, meaning turned toward, from ob- and vertere, to turn; the observer-facing sense developed into the principal face of a coin and later a contrasting counterpart. [Etymology and senses: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/obverse)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 obverse 作为完整词干使用；obverse + -ly → obversely（正面朝向地；相反地）。历史构词可分析为 ob-（朝向）+ vers-（转）；相关词有 obvert（使转向；逻辑学中使换质）和 obversion（换质），后两者属于专门用语，并非 obverse 的普通后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, obverse normally functions as a whole stem: obverse + -ly → obversely. Its historical elements are ob-, toward, and vers-, turn; related technical words include obvert and obversion, which are not ordinary suffix derivatives of obverse.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: front（正面）是日常通称；heads（硬币的人像面）主要用于钱币，尤其用于抛硬币；opposite（相反事物）对应抽象义，适用范围比 obverse 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Front is the everyday term for a principal face; heads refers to the portrait side of a coin, especially in coin tossing; opposite matches the abstract sense but has a much broader range of uses.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Turned toward you means the front; paired with another side, it can also mean the contrasting counterpart.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语经盎格鲁法语借入此词，其源头是拉丁语 phantasma 和希腊语 phantasma（显现之物、幻象），与 phantazein（使显现于眼前或心中）有关。表示“显现的形象”的词义，由此发展为幽灵般的幻影和想象中的虚像。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/phantasm)
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed the word through Anglo-French from Latin phantasma and ultimately Greek phantasma, an apparition, related to phantazein, to present to the eye or mind. This connection with appearance underlies its senses of a ghostly figure and an imagined image. [Etymology: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/phantasm)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 phantasm 作为完整词干：phantasm + -al → phantasmal（幻影般的），phantasmal + -ly → phantasmally（如幻影般地），phantasm + -ic → phantasmic（幻象的）。扩展词族包括 phantasmagoria（变幻不定的一连串幻象）、phantasmagoric／phantasmagorical（幻象纷呈的）及 phantasmagorically（如变幻的幻象般地）；phantom（幻影）和 fantasy（幻想）是历史同源词，并非直接后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat phantasm as a whole modern stem: phantasm + -al → phantasmal; phantasmal + -ly → phantasmally; phantasm + -ic → phantasmic. The extended family includes phantasmagoria, phantasmagoric, phantasmagorical, and phantasmagorically; phantom and fantasy are historical relatives rather than direct suffix derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: apparition（幽灵般的显现）突出突然出现、仿佛看得见的形象；illusion（错觉、假象）强调感知或判断受到误导；figment（虚构之物）强调完全由想象产生。phantasm 带文学色彩，兼有幻影与想象产物两层意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Apparition emphasizes a seemingly visible, often ghostly appearance; illusion emphasizes misleading perception or belief; figment emphasizes something invented by the imagination. Phantasm is literary and can suggest either a spectral image or an imagined creation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“显现”：眼前似有形，现实却无物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to appearance: a vivid image appears, but nothing solid is there.

etymology_story.zh: 该动物名经新拉丁语 Rhesus 而来，借用了希腊神话中特拉基亚国王 Rhēsos 的名字。它属于专名转成动物名称，不能根据猴子的外形或习性拆解其字母来解释。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rhesus)
etymology_story.en: The animal name comes through New Latin Rhesus from Rhēsos, a mythical king of Thrace. It is a borrowed proper name rather than a descriptive formation based on the monkey's appearance or behavior. [Etymology: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rhesus)

morphology_enriched.zh: rhesus 是不可按现代常用词缀拆分的完整借词；复数为 rhesuses。常见组合有 rhesus monkey 和 rhesus macaque；血型术语中另见 Rhesus factor／Rh factor（Rh 因子）及 rhesus-positive／rhesus-negative（Rh 阳性的／阴性的）。这些组合中的前置修饰用法不构成 rhesus 的普通独立形容词词义；该词没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Rhesus is an unsegmented loanword in modern English; its plural is rhesuses. Common combinations include rhesus monkey and rhesus macaque; blood-group terminology also includes Rhesus factor or Rh factor and rhesus-positive or rhesus-negative. These modifying uses do not establish a separate common adjective sense, and the word has no usual derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rhesus monkey 和 rhesus macaque 都是该物种的完整名称，与 rhesus 指同一种动物；macaque（猕猴）范围更广，包括多个物种，不能在需要精确区分物种时直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rhesus monkey and rhesus macaque are full names for the same species. Macaque is broader and covers multiple species, so it is not interchangeable when species-level precision matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 神话人名借给猴子：整体记 rhesus＝恒河猴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A mythological name became a monkey's name: remember rhesus as one whole label.

morphology_enriched.en: Trilby is a whole stem converted from a proper name, not a modern combination of tril- and -by. Its plural is trilbies, with final y replaced by -ies; trilby hat is a common combination, while the rare derivative trilbied means wearing a trilby.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: A fedora is similar but typically has a wider brim; felt hat names a broader category by material; snap-brim hat names a broader category by brim construction rather than this particular style.

etymology_story.zh: GPA 是 grade point average 的首字母缩略形式，形成于以绩点汇总课程成绩的美国教育用语。它后来成为国际教育交流中常用的学业成绩术语。[缩略形式依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/GPA)
etymology_story.en: GPA abbreviates grade point average, an expression associated with American educational grading. It subsequently became widely used in international discussion of academic records. [Expansion: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/GPA)

morphology_enriched.zh: grade（成绩等级）+ point（点数）+ average（平均值）→ grade point average → GPA；这是逐字母读出的首字母缩略语。复数为 GPAs，不加撇号；常见组合包括 cumulative GPA（累计平均绩点）、semester GPA（学期平均绩点）、weighted GPA（加权平均绩点）和 unweighted GPA（未加权平均绩点），没有常用的后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Grade + point + average → grade point average → GPA, an initialism pronounced letter by letter. Its plural is GPAs without an apostrophe; common combinations include cumulative GPA, semester GPA, weighted GPA, and unweighted GPA, with no usual suffix derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grade point average 是 GPA 的完整形式，意义相同；average grade（平均成绩）是近义表达，但不一定采用绩点制；academic average（学业平均成绩）范围较宽，具体计算方式取决于教育制度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grade point average is the exact expanded equivalent; average grade is a near-synonym that need not use grade points; academic average is broader, with its calculation depending on the educational system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: G＝成绩，P＝点数，A＝平均：把成绩换成点，再取平均。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Grades → Points → Average: convert grades to points, then average them.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语源构词成分组成的现代科学词：ōion（也转写为 ōon）意为“卵”，kytos 原意为“中空容器”，后来用于表示“细胞”。该词因此表示正在发育的卵细胞。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines elements derived from Greek ōion, also transliterated as ōon, meaning 'egg', and kytos, meaning 'hollow vessel' and later used for 'cell'. It names a developing egg cell.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：oo-（卵）+ -cyte（细胞）→ oocyte（卵母细胞）。词族包括复数 oocytes，以及专业形容词 oocytic（卵母细胞的）；oogenesis（卵子发生）、oogonium（卵原细胞）和 ovum（成熟卵细胞）是相关术语，并非 oocyte 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: oo- ('egg') + -cyte ('cell') → oocyte. Its family includes the plural oocytes and the technical adjective oocytic. Oogenesis, oogonium, and ovum are related terms rather than direct derivatives of oocyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: egg cell（卵细胞）是较通俗、范围较宽的说法；ovum（成熟卵细胞）通常强调已经成熟的雌配子；female germ cell（雌性生殖细胞）涵盖更多发育阶段。oocyte 特指卵子发育过程中尚未完成成熟分裂的细胞。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Egg cell is a broader, less technical expression; ovum usually emphasizes the mature female gamete; female germ cell covers a wider range of developmental stages. Oocyte specifically identifies a developing egg cell before its maturation divisions are complete.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: oo- 是“卵”，-cyte 是“细胞”：记住一枚仍在成熟中的卵细胞。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Oo- means 'egg' and -cyte means 'cell': picture an egg cell still maturing.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自意大利语 operetta，是 opera（歌剧）的小称形式，字面意思是“小歌剧”。它后来成为一种通常题材轻松、融合歌唱与对白的音乐戏剧体裁名称。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Italian operetta, a diminutive of opera, literally meaning 'little opera'. It became the name of a musical theatre genre typically combining a light story with singing and spoken dialogue.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：意大利语 oper-（opera 去掉末尾 -a）+ -etta（小称后缀）→ operetta；英语将其整体借入。词族包括 operettas（复数）、operettist（轻歌剧作家或作曲家）和较少见的 operettic（轻歌剧的）；opera（歌剧）与 operatic（歌剧的）属于相关基础词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation in Italian: oper- (opera without its final -a) + -etta (a diminutive suffix) → operetta; English borrowed the whole word. Its family includes operettas, operettist, and the less common adjective operettic. Opera and operatic belong to the related base family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: light opera（轻歌剧）与 operetta 最接近；comic opera（喜歌剧）强调喜剧性，但并非总与轻歌剧属于同一体裁；musical（音乐剧）范围更广，音乐风格和演唱传统也可能不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Light opera is the closest equivalent; comic opera emphasizes comedy but does not always identify the same genre; musical is broader and may involve different musical styles and vocal traditions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: opera 加“小称”后缀：一部气氛更轻快的“小歌剧”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Opera plus a diminutive ending: a 'little opera' with a lighter touch.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 solénoïde 进入英语，法语术语由安培用希腊语 sōlēn（管）和表示“形状、样式”的成分构成。它最初指管状线圈，后来也指利用这种线圈驱动机械部件的装置。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French solénoïde, a term coined by Ampère from Greek sōlēn, meaning 'tube', and an element meaning 'form' or 'shape'. Its meaning extended from a tubular coil to a device that uses such a coil to move a mechanical part.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：solen-（管，希腊语源词干）+ -oid（形似……的）→ solenoid。词族包括 solenoids（复数）、solenoidal（螺线管的；数学中指无散度的）和 solenoidally（以螺线管方式；以无散度方式）；solenoid valve（电磁阀）是常用复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: solen- (a Greek-derived stem meaning 'tube') + -oid ('resembling') → solenoid. Its family includes solenoids, solenoidal ('relating to a solenoid', or 'divergence-free' in mathematics), and solenoidally. Solenoid valve is a common compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coil（线圈）只说明绕制结构，不一定呈管状或用于电磁驱动；electromagnet（电磁铁）强调通电产生磁性；electromagnetic actuator（电磁执行器）强调产生机械运动，是装置义 solenoid 所属的更大类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coil describes a winding without necessarily implying a tubular shape or electromagnetic operation; electromagnet emphasizes magnetism produced by electricity; electromagnetic actuator emphasizes mechanical movement and is a broader category containing the device sense of solenoid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: solen- 是“管”：电线绕成管，通电产生磁场，还能推动铁芯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Solen- means 'tube': wire forms a tube, electricity creates magnetism, and the magnetism can move a core.

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自印地语和乌尔都语 kauṛī，可追溯至梵语 kapardikā，后者与 kaparda（宝螺壳）有关。由于这类贝壳曾被广泛用作货币和装饰品，英语 cowrie 既指动物，也指它的壳。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Hindi and Urdu kauṛī and can be traced to Sanskrit kapardikā, related to kaparda, meaning 'cowrie shell'. Because these shells were widely used as money and ornaments, English cowrie names both the animal and its shell.

morphology_enriched.zh: cowrie 在现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的借词，不能分析为 cow + 后缀。词形包括另一拼写 cowry，以及两种拼写共用的复数 cowries；没有常用的直接派生词，常见复合词包括 cowrie shell（宝螺壳）、cowrie money（贝币）和 cowrie-shell necklace（宝螺壳项链）。
morphology_enriched.en: Cowrie is an unanalyzable loanword in modern English; it is not cow plus a suffix. Its forms include the alternative spelling cowry and the shared plural cowries. It has no common direct derivatives; compounds include cowrie shell, cowrie money, and cowrie-shell necklace.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sea snail（海螺）是动物义的上位词，范围远大于 cowrie；seashell（海贝壳）泛指海生软体动物的壳；shell money（贝币）强调贝壳的货币用途，也可能使用宝螺以外的贝壳。三者都不是 cowrie 在所有语境中的完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sea snail is a broader term for the animal; seashell refers generally to the shell of a marine mollusc; shell money emphasizes monetary use and may involve shells other than cowries. None is interchangeable with cowrie in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一枚光亮的小贝壳：海里是宝螺，串起来是饰品，过去还能当钱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one glossy little shell: a snail's home, a necklace ornament, and once a piece of money.

senses.meaning_zh: 文雅；被视为体现良好教养或较高社会身份的举止与气派，有时含装腔意味
senses.meaning_en: Refined manners or appearance associated with good breeding or high social status, sometimes suggesting affectation.
senses.english_definition: Gentility is the quality of behaving or appearing in a polite and refined way that suggests a high social position.
senses.collocation_en: an air of gentility; shabby gentility
senses.collocation_zh: 文雅的气派；清贫却仍维持体面的派头
senses.sentence_en: Despite her reduced income, she maintained an air of gentility.
senses.sentence_zh: 尽管收入减少，她仍保持着文雅体面的气派。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由中古英语从古法语 gentilité 借入，源自拉丁语 gentilitas，最初与氏族或家族归属有关。其意义后来从出身和社会身份转向被认为体现良好教养的举止，有时也暗含刻意维持体面的意味。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed the word from Old French gentilité, ultimately from Latin gentilitas, originally associated with membership of a clan or family. Its meaning developed from birth and social standing to manners thought to show good breeding, sometimes with a suggestion of affected respectability.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可识别的结构是 gentil-（与 gentle、genteel 同源的词干）+ -ity（性质或状态）；但 gentility 是整体借入英语的词，不能简单视为现代英语 gentle 临时加后缀而成。同源词族包括 gentle（温和的；文雅的）、gently（温和地）、gentleness（温和）、genteel（讲究体面的；文雅的）、genteelly（文雅地）和 genteelness（文雅；体面）。
morphology_enriched.en: Its recognizable structure is gentil- (a stem related to gentle and genteel) + -ity ('quality or state'), although gentility was borrowed as a whole rather than newly formed from modern English gentle. Its related family includes gentle, gently, gentleness, genteel, genteelly, and genteelness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: refinement（文雅；精致）强调品味和举止经过陶冶；politeness（礼貌）强调待人的礼节，不暗示社会阶层；genteelness（文雅；讲究体面）最接近 gentility，也可能带有刻意做派的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Refinement emphasizes cultivated taste and manners; politeness emphasizes courteous treatment of others without implying social class; genteelness is closest to gentility and can likewise suggest a deliberate display of respectability.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“好出身”到“好教养”：gentility 是举止中流露或刻意维持的文雅体面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From 'good birth' to 'good breeding': gentility is refinement displayed or carefully maintained.

senses.meaning_zh: 反复恳求；纠缠着请求
senses.meaning_en: to ask persistently and annoyingly
senses.english_definition: If you importune someone, you repeatedly ask them to do something, often until they become annoyed.
senses.collocation_en: importune someone for money; importune someone to help
senses.collocation_zh: 纠缠着向某人要钱；反复恳求某人帮忙
senses.sentence_en: He kept importuning his relatives for money until they stopped answering his calls.
senses.sentence_zh: 他不断纠缠亲戚向他们要钱，直到他们不再接他的电话。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 importuner 传入英语，源于拉丁语 importunus，意为“不合时宜的、令人厌烦的”。英语中的动词义逐渐集中于令人不胜其烦地反复请求。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French importuner, ultimately from Latin importunus, meaning inconvenient or troublesome. Its English verb meaning became focused on troubling someone with persistent requests.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，importune 通常作为整体动词词干处理，不宜拆成具有现代意义的 im- + portune。屈折形式：importunes、importuned、importuning；相关词族：importunate（纠缠不休的）、importunately（纠缠不休地）、importunity（反复恳求；纠缠），以及较少见的 importuner（纠缠着请求的人）。这些词族成员共享历史词干，并非全部由现代 importune 直接加后缀形成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, importune is normally treated as a whole verb stem rather than as a transparent combination of im- and portune. Inflections are importunes, importuned, and importuning; related family members include importunate, importunately, importunity, and the less common importuner. These words share a historical stem rather than all being straightforward modern suffix formations from importune.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: implore（恳求）强调迫切而强烈的情感；beseech（恳求、哀求）语体较正式，强调诚挚请求；pester（纠缠、烦扰）强调反复打扰，未必是在恳求。importune 兼有反复请求和令人厌烦两层意思，语体较正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Implore emphasizes urgent emotion; beseech is formal and stresses earnest pleading; pester emphasizes repeated annoyance without necessarily involving a serious appeal. Importune combines persistent requesting with unwelcome pressure and is relatively formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从历史上的“令人厌烦”联想到“请求一遍又一遍，直到对方烦”：反复恳求。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical idea of being troublesome with asking again and again until the listener is annoyed.

etymology_story.zh: irredeemable 由否定前缀加 redeemable 构成。redeem 经法语源于拉丁语 redimere，原意为“买回、赎回”，后来扩展为“拯救、补救”，因此 irredeemable 既可指不能赎回，也可指无法挽救。
etymology_story.en: Irredeemable was formed by adding a negative prefix to redeemable. Redeem came through French from Latin redimere, meaning to buy back, and later developed the senses of saving or making amends, which explain the adjective's financial and figurative meanings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：ir-（否定前缀 in- 在 r 前的同化形式）+ redeem（赎回；挽救）+ -able（能够被……的）。直接派生词：irredeemably（无可挽救地）、irredeemability（不可挽救性；不可赎回性）、较少见的 irredeemableness（不可挽救的性质）。相关词族：redeems、redeemed、redeeming、redeemer（救赎者）、redeemable（可赎回的；可挽救的）、redeemability（可赎回性）、redemption（赎回；救赎）、redemptive（具有救赎作用的）、redemptively（以具有救赎作用的方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ir-, the assimilated form of negative in- before r, + redeem + -able. Direct derivatives are irredeemably, irredeemability, and the less common irredeemableness. Related family members include redeems, redeemed, redeeming, redeemer, redeemable, redeemability, redemption, redemptive, and redemptively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: irreparable（无法修复的）强调损害无法修补；incorrigible（屡教不改的）主要形容人的行为或习惯；hopeless（无望的）泛指没有成功或改善的希望。irredeemable 强调无法挽救、弥补或恢复价值，也可带诙谐语气形容根深蒂固的性格。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Irreparable focuses on damage that cannot be repaired; incorrigible usually describes behavior or habits that resist correction; hopeless broadly suggests no prospect of success or improvement. Irredeemable emphasizes the impossibility of rescue, compensation, or restored worth, and can humorously describe a deeply rooted personality trait.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: redeem 是“赎回来、救回来”；ir- 加上去，就是“再也赎不回、救不回”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Redeem means buy back or save; ir- closes off that possibility: it cannot be bought back or saved.

etymology_story.zh: limpid 来自拉丁语 limpidus，意为“清澈、透明”。清水一眼可见其底的形象，后来被用于形容清晰易懂的语言和表达。
etymology_story.en: Limpid comes from Latin limpidus, meaning clear or transparent. The image of water that can easily be seen through was extended to language and expression whose meaning is readily understood.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，limpid 通常作为整体形容词词干处理，不宜把 limp 当作其词根。派生词：limpid + -ly → limpidly（清澈地；清晰流畅地）；limpid + -ity → limpidity（清澈；明晰）；limpid + -ness → limpidness（清澈；明晰，较少见）。比较级和最高级通常用 more limpid、most limpid。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, limpid is normally treated as a whole adjective stem; limp is not its root. Derivatives are limpid + -ly → limpidly, limpid + -ity → limpidity, and limpid + -ness → the less common limpidness. Comparison normally uses more limpid and most limpid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clear（清澈的；清楚的）最通用；transparent（透明的）强调光线能够透过；lucid（清晰易懂的）主要强调思想、解释或文风明白。limpid 较具文学色彩，常同时带有清澈、纯净或流畅之美。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clear is the broadest everyday term; transparent emphasizes the passage of light; lucid chiefly describes understandable thought, explanation, or writing. Limpid is more literary and often suggests an attractive purity or graceful clarity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 水清得看得到底，文章清楚得看得到意思：两种“清澈”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: See through the water to its bottom; see through the prose to its meaning: physical clarity becomes verbal clarity.

etymology_story.zh: mayday 在20世纪20年代被创作并采用为无线电遇险呼号，其读音依据法语 m'aider，见于 venez m'aider（来帮助我）。它与 May Day（五一节）的拼写相似只是巧合，词源并非 may 加 day。
etymology_story.en: Mayday was coined and adopted as a radio distress call in the 1920s, based on the sound of French m'aider in venez m'aider, meaning come and help me. Its resemblance to May Day is coincidental; it was not formed from the English words may and day.

morphology_enriched.zh: mayday 是不可按现代英语成分拆解的借音词，兼作名词和感叹词。名词复数为 maydays；常见复合表达有 mayday call（遇险呼叫）、mayday signal（遇险信号）、mayday message（遇险报文）。没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Mayday is a phonetic borrowing that cannot be meaningfully divided into modern English components, and it functions as both a noun and an interjection. Its noun plural is maydays; common combinations include mayday call, mayday signal, and mayday message. It has no established family of common derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: distress call（遇险呼叫）是各种遇险呼救的通称；SOS（国际求救信号）可指传统编码求救信号，也常泛指求助；cry for help（求救声；求助行为）适用范围最广。mayday 特指国际无线电话遇险呼号，也可指含有该呼号的呼叫。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Distress call is a general term for a call reporting grave danger; SOS names a traditional coded distress signal and is also used broadly for an appeal for help; cry for help is the widest everyday expression. Mayday specifically names the international radiotelephony distress word or a call using it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 mayday 的声音连到法语 m'aider：“帮助我！”——无线电里的紧急呼救。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the sound of mayday to French m'aider, help me: a plea for help becomes a radio distress call.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“整洁时髦”的 natty 至迟在18世纪末已见于英语，其更早来源并不确定，后来也用于形容精巧实用的东西。健身俚语中的 natty 则是 natural 的缩略形式，属于另一条构词来源。
etymology_story.en: Natty meaning neat and stylish is recorded by the late eighteenth century, although its earlier origin is uncertain; it later also described neatly useful things. The bodybuilding slang natty is a shortening of natural and has a separate formation history.

morphology_enriched.zh: “整洁时髦”义的 natty 在现代英语中通常作为整体词干处理：natty → nattier、nattiest；natty + -ly → nattily（整洁时髦地）；natty + -ness → nattiness（整洁时髦），加后缀时 y 变 i。健身义的 natty 由 natural 截短并以 -y 结尾，可作形容词，也可通过词类转换作可数名词，复数为 natties。
morphology_enriched.en: Natty meaning stylish is normally treated as a whole modern stem: its comparative and superlative are nattier and nattiest, and its derivatives are nattily and nattiness, with y changing to i before the suffix. The bodybuilding term is a shortening of natural with a -y ending; it functions as an adjective and, through conversion, a count noun with the plural natties.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 穿着义：dapper（衣着整洁讲究的）尤常形容男性；smart（整洁精神的）用途更广；stylish（时髦的）侧重风格与品位。natty 常带有利落、精致的赞许意味。器物义接近 neat（精巧实用的）；健身义接近 natural（天然训练的），名词可释为 natural bodybuilder（天然健美者）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For appearance, dapper especially describes neatly dressed men, smart has a broader sense of polished presentation, and stylish emphasizes fashion or taste; natty often approvingly suggests a trim, well-chosen look. For devices, neat is close in meaning. In bodybuilding, natural is the corresponding adjective, and natural bodybuilder paraphrases the noun.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 普通义记“衣服利落，工具精巧”；健身义直接连到 natural：“天然练出来的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the ordinary senses, picture a neat outfit or a clever little gadget; for gym slang, connect natty directly with natural.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于拉丁语 probitas“善良、正直”，其基础是 probus“良好的、正直的”，并与法语 probité 同源。英语保留了强调道德操守的含义，尤其常用于公共事务和财务行为。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin probitas, meaning goodness or uprightness, based on probus, meaning good or honest, and is related to French probité. English retained its emphasis on moral integrity, particularly in public and financial affairs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 probity 作为整体借词学习；从历史结构看，可分析为 prob-（良好、正直）＋名词后缀 -ity（性质）。直接对应词有 improbity（不诚实、不正直，罕用）；prove、probe、probable、probative 和 approbation 属于更广的历史同源词群，并非 probity 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, probity is generally learned as a whole borrowed word; historically, it contains prob- meaning good or upright and the noun suffix -ity. Its direct counterpart is the uncommon improbity; prove, probe, probable, probative, and approbation belong to the wider historical family rather than being direct derivatives of probity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: integrity 强调始终坚持道德原则；honesty 强调真实、不欺骗；rectitude 强调行为在道德上的端正。probity 较正式，尤其突出值得信赖的公共或职业操守。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Integrity emphasizes consistent adherence to moral principles; honesty emphasizes truthfulness and freedom from deception; rectitude emphasizes morally correct conduct. Probity is formal and particularly suggests trustworthy public or professional conduct.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史词根 prob- 的“良好、正直”：probity 就是品行端正这一品质。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect historical prob-, meaning good or upright, with the quality of upright character.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在17世纪仿照 subordinate“下级的”形成，以 super-“在……之上”替换 sub-“在……之下”。后半部分最终联系拉丁语 ordinare“排列、安排”，后来也用于语言学中的类别层级。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the seventeenth century on the model of subordinate, replacing sub-, meaning below, with super-, meaning above. Its second element ultimately relates to Latin ordinare, meaning to arrange, and the word later acquired a specialized use in linguistic classification.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：super-（在……之上）＋ordinate（与排列、次序有关的词基）。词族包括 superordination（上位关系、上位安排）和 superordinately（以上位方式，罕用）；对应词包括 subordinate、subordination 和 coordinate。形容词、名词的词尾读 /nət/，动词的词尾读 /neɪt/。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is super-, meaning above, plus ordinate, a base associated with arrangement or order. The family includes superordination and the rare superordinately; corresponding formations include subordinate, subordination, and coordinate. The adjective and noun end in /nət/, while the verb ends in /neɪt/.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: superior 泛指地位更高，也可指质量更好；higher-level 强调层级位置，表达较通俗；hypernym 专指语言学中的上位词。superordinate 突出明确的等级或类别包含关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Superior can mean higher in rank or better in quality; higher-level is a more accessible description of hierarchical position; hypernym specifically names a broader term in linguistics. Superordinate emphasizes an explicit ranking or category-inclusion relationship.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super-＝在上方，ordinate＝排列：排列在上一层，就是上位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Super- means above: something superordinate sits one level higher in an ordered structure.

etymology_story.zh: 该词兴起于19世纪30年代英国的禁酒运动，tee 是字母 t 的读音，用来加强 total“完全的”，强调彻底戒酒。它与 tea“茶”没有词源关系。
etymology_story.en: The word emerged in the British temperance movement of the 1830s, with tee, the spoken name of the letter t, intensifying total to emphasize complete abstinence. It has no etymological connection with tea.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：tee-（以字母 t 的读音加强语气）＋total（完全的），但 tee- 不是现代英语中能自由造词的普通前缀。主要词族有 teetotaller（完全不饮酒者，英式拼写）、teetotaler（美式拼写）和 teetotalism（完全戒酒的主张或实践）。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is emphatic tee-, representing the spoken letter t, plus total; tee- is not an ordinary productive prefix in modern English. The main family members are teetotaller in British spelling, teetotaler in American spelling, and teetotalism, the principle or practice of complete abstinence from alcohol.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: abstinent 强调主动克制，范围不限于酒；sober 可仅指当下没有醉，也可指持续戒酒；non-drinking 直接表示不饮酒，语气较中性。teetotal 明确表示完全不喝酒。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Abstinent emphasizes deliberate restraint and need not concern alcohol; sober can mean currently not intoxicated or maintaining abstinence; non-drinking is a neutral description. Teetotal explicitly means drinking no alcohol at all.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 total“完全”再强调一次：完全戒酒，一滴不喝。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of an extra-emphatic total: total abstinence means no alcohol at all.

morphology_enriched.zh: 纹章学的 vert 是整体借词，没有现代英语中的可拆分词缀；verdant（翠绿的）、verdancy（翠绿、青翠）和 verdure（青翠草木）是历史同源词，并非由 vert 直接派生。运动义是 vertical 的截短形式，常构成 vert skating、vert ramp 和 vert skater。
morphology_enriched.en: Heraldic vert is a whole borrowed word without productive English affixes; verdant, verdancy, and verdure are historical relatives rather than direct derivatives. The sports sense is a clipping of vertical and appears in compounds such as vert skating, vert ramp, and vert skater.

morphology_enriched.zh: vulva 是整体借词；复数为 vulvas 或 vulvae。派生与组合常用词干 vulv- 或组合形式 vulvo-：vulval、vulvar（外阴的），vulvitis（外阴炎），vulvovaginal（外阴阴道的），vulvovaginitis（外阴阴道炎），vulvodynia（外阴痛），vulvectomy（外阴切除术），vulvoplasty（外阴成形术）和 vulvoscopy（外阴镜检查）。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“泉源”的 fount 是 fountain 的缩略形式，最终源自拉丁语 fons（属格 fontis）“泉”；泉水涌出的形象后来引申为知识等的来源。印刷义属于另一条词源，来自法语 fonte“铸造、铸成的一套字”，与拉丁语 fundere“倾注、熔铸”有关。
etymology_story.en: Fount meaning “spring” is a shortening of fountain, ultimately from Latin fons, genitive fontis, meaning “spring”; flowing water supplied the metaphor for a source of knowledge or other qualities. The printing sense has a separate origin in French fonte, referring to casting or a set of cast type, related to Latin fundere, “to pour or cast.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，fount 是不可再作生产性拆分的单纯词，复数为 founts。“泉源”义与 fountain（泉、喷泉）、fountainhead（源头）有词源联系，但二者不是在现代英语中给 fount 加词缀形成的。印刷义的拼写变体为 font；常用搭配有 fount of wisdom 和 fount of type。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fount is a simple word with no productive internal affixes; its plural is founts. In the source sense, fountain and fountainhead are historically related words, rather than modern derivatives formed by adding affixes to fount. The printing sense has the spelling variant font; established combinations include fount of wisdom and fount of type.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: source（来源）最中性、适用范围最广；wellspring（源泉）也可比喻丰富而持续的来源；fountain（泉、喷泉）更常指实际的水景。fount 的来源义较有文学色彩，也可用于幽默表达；印刷义对应 font，而 typeface 指字体设计，不专指一副铅字。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Source is neutral and broadly applicable; wellspring suggests an abundant, continuing source; fountain more often denotes an actual water feature. Fount sounds literary and can also be humorous; in printing, its equivalent is font, whereas typeface denotes the design rather than a particular set of type.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 知识像泉水一样不断涌出：fount＝源泉；印刷义另记“把金属浇铸成一副字”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture knowledge bubbling up like spring water: a fount is a source. For printing, picture metal poured into a complete set of type.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 livre 借自法语，作为货币名称可追溯至拉丁语 libra“磅”。它体现了早期记账货币与贵金属重量的历史联系，后来成为法国长期使用的货币及记账单位。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed livre from French, whose monetary term descends from Latin libra, meaning “pound.” The name reflects the historical connection between units of account and weights of precious metal, and it became a long-established French monetary unit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 livre 是完整借入的单纯名词，不能拆成英语词根与词缀；复数为 livres，没有常用的英语派生词族。livre tournois（图尔里弗）和 livre parisis（巴黎里弗）是历史名称，其中修饰语分别表示与图尔和巴黎有关。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, livre is a borrowed simple noun, with no English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is livres, and it has no established productive family of English derivatives. Livre tournois and livre parisis are historical names whose modifiers refer to Tours and Paris respectively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: French pound（法国磅）可用于解释 livre 的历史名称；unit of account（记账单位）说明其核算功能；currency unit（货币单位）是上位概念。这些表达并非在所有历史语境中都能直接替换 livre，也不能把 livre 等同于 franc（法郎）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: French pound is an explanatory rendering of the historical name; unit of account describes its accounting function; currency unit is a broader category. These expressions are not interchangeable with livre in every historical context, and a livre should not be equated with a franc.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“磅重”想到“按重量计钱”：livre 是法国历史上的“钱磅”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect a pound of weight with money measured by weight: the livre was France’s historical monetary “pound.”

etymology_story.zh: minima 保留了拉丁语 minimum 的中性复数形式；minimum 来自 minimus，意为“最小的、最少的”。英语沿用这一古典复数，尤其常见于数学、科学及正式文体。
etymology_story.en: Minima preserves the Latin neuter plural of minimum, derived from minimus, meaning “smallest” or “least.” English retained this classical plural, particularly in mathematics, science, and formal writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: minimum → minima：这是拉丁式屈折复数，词尾 -um 变为 -a，不是现代英语中普遍适用的派生规则；minimums 也是英语复数形式。常见相关词族包括 minimum（最低限度）、minimal（极少的）、minimally（最低程度地）、minimalism（极简主义）、minimalist（极简主义者；极简的）、minimalistic（极简风格的）、minimize/minimise（使最小化）、minimization/minimisation（最小化）和 minimizer/minimiser（使某量最小的对象或工具）。
morphology_enriched.en: Minimum → minima is a Latin-style inflectional plural, replacing -um with -a, rather than a generally productive English derivational rule; minimums is also an English plural. The established related family includes minimum, minimal, minimally, minimalism, minimalist, minimalistic, minimize/minimise, minimization/minimisation, and minimizer/minimiser.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: minimums 是同一单数的另一复数形式，在一般用法中常可替换 minima；lows（低点、最低值）较日常；lower bounds（下界）在数学中指不大于集合中任何元素的界限，不一定能被实际取到，因此不一定是最小值。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Minimums is an alternative plural of the same singular and is often interchangeable with minima in general use; lows is less formal. Lower bounds are mathematical limits no greater than any member of a set, but they need not be attained and therefore need not be minima.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 privet 是不可再拆的单纯植物名，没有可靠的英语词根加词缀分析；作可数名词时复数为 privets，也可作集合或物质性用法。常见组合有 privet hedge（女贞绿篱）和 privet shrub（女贞灌木），没有常用的派生词族；它与 private 没有已确立的词源联系。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, privet is a simple plant name with no reliable root-and-affix breakdown. Its count plural is privets, and it also has collective or mass uses. Common combinations include privet hedge and privet shrub; there is no established productive derivative family, and no established etymological connection with private.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ligustrum is the corresponding botanical genus name; hedge shrub is a broader category that includes privet; hedge denotes the planted barrier rather than a particular plant. Privet covers multiple species and should not automatically be equated with a single species.

etymology_story.zh: 英语形容词 recherché 借自法语 rechercher“仔细寻找”的过去分词，字面意思是“经过搜寻的”。“费心搜求”引申为“精心挑选、精雅罕见”，也可带有“刻意考究、过分求奇”的批评意味；recherche 是英语中省略重音符号的拼写。
etymology_story.en: The English adjective recherché comes from the past participle of French rechercher, “to seek carefully,” literally describing something sought out. This developed into “carefully selected, refined, or rare,” sometimes with criticism of excessive sophistication; recherche is the English spelling without the accent.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 recherche/recherché 是整体借入的形容词，没有常用的生产性英语派生词族。历史上的法语构词可分析为 re-（此处有加强意味）+ chercher（寻找）→ rechercher，其过去分词为 recherché；这不是现代英语中的直接构词过程，普通英语通常用 refined、sophisticated 或 obscure 等词表达相关概念。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, recherche/recherché is a borrowed adjective with no common productive family of English derivatives. Historically, French re- has an intensive role in re- + chercher, “to seek,” forming rechercher, whose past participle is recherché; this is French historical formation, not a productive English construction.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: refined（精雅的）强调品味和细致；esoteric（少数人懂的）强调知识或兴趣圈子的局限；rarefied（高深小众的）强调远离日常经验的精英化氛围。recherché 把罕见、精挑细选和考究结合起来，有时暗含做作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Refined emphasizes taste and delicacy; esoteric emphasizes knowledge or interests understood by a limited group; rarefied suggests an exclusive intellectual or cultural atmosphere. Recherché combines rarity, careful selection, and sophistication, sometimes implying affectation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 费心“搜求”来的东西，往往精雅少见；搜求过头，就显得刻意。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Something carefully sought out may be rare and refined; taking that search too far can seem affected.

senses.meaning_zh: 视网膜病；视网膜病变
senses.meaning_en: disease or damage affecting the retina
senses.english_definition: Retinopathy is a condition in which the retina at the back of the eye becomes diseased or damaged.

senses.collocation_zh: 糖尿病视网膜病变；早产儿视网膜病变

etymology_story.zh: 该医学词由表示“视网膜”的组合形式 retin/o 与源自希腊语、表示“疾病”的 -pathy 构成。Retina 来自中世纪拉丁语，字面有“小网”之意，用来描述眼内这层呈网状的组织。
etymology_story.en: This medical term combines retin/o, meaning “retina,” with -pathy, a Greek-derived element meaning “disease.” Retina comes from Medieval Latin and literally means “little net,” describing the netlike tissue inside the eye.

morphology_enriched.zh: retin/o（视网膜）+ -pathy（疾病）→ retinopathy；复数为 retinopathies。直接派生词：retinopathic（视网膜病变的）；同词根词：retina（视网膜）、retinal（视网膜的）、retinitis（视网膜炎）。
morphology_enriched.en: retin/o (retina) + -pathy (disease) → retinopathy; plural: retinopathies. Direct derivative: retinopathic (relating to retinopathy). Related root-family words: retina, retinal (relating to the retina), and retinitis (inflammation of the retina).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: retinal disease（视网膜疾病）是最接近的通俗释义；retinal damage（视网膜损伤）强调组织受损；retinal disorder（视网膜疾患）范围较宽，也可包括并非典型病变的异常情况。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Retinal disease is the closest plain-language equivalent; retinal damage emphasizes tissue injury; retinal disorder is broader and can include abnormalities beyond established disease.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: retin/o 指眼底的“感光网”，-pathy 指疾病：感光网生病，就是视网膜病变。
mnemonic_anchor.en: retin/o names the eye’s light-sensitive “net”; -pathy means disease: disease of that net is retinopathy.

senses.english_definition: If you underplay something, you describe or present it as less important or serious than it really is.

senses.meaning_zh: 以克制、含蓄的方式表演
senses.meaning_en: to perform a role or scene with restrained expression
senses.english_definition: If an actor underplays a role or scene, they perform it without showing strong or exaggerated emotion.
senses.collocation_en: underplay a role; underplay a scene
senses.collocation_zh: 含蓄地演绎角色；克制地表演一场戏

etymology_story.zh: Underplay 由 under- 与 play 构成，早期用于纸牌，指手中有大牌却先出小牌。后来它用于描述克制的舞台表演，并进一步发展为“淡化重要性或严重性”。
etymology_story.en: Underplay combines under- and play and was first used in card playing for playing a lower card while holding a higher one. It later described restrained acting and then developed the broader meaning of making something seem less important or serious.

morphology_enriched.zh: under-（低于通常程度；不足）+ play（打牌；表演）→ underplay。屈折形式：underplays、underplayed、underplaying；underplayed 也可作形容词，表示“被淡化的；表演克制的”。对应词为 overplay（夸大；表演过火）。
morphology_enriched.en: under- (below the usual degree; insufficiently) + play (play cards; perform) → underplay. Inflected forms: underplays, underplayed, underplaying. Underplayed also functions adjectivally, meaning understated or restrained in performance. The contrasting formation is overplay.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: downplay（淡化）常指降低他人对某事重要性的认识；understate（轻描淡写）侧重措辞或陈述低于实际程度；play down（淡化）是日常表达，意义与 underplay 的一般义接近，但通常不表示克制表演。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Downplay commonly means reducing the importance people attach to something; understate focuses on wording or presentation that falls below the reality; play down is an everyday equivalent of the general sense but does not usually describe restrained acting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: under + play：把表现的“音量”调低，既可淡化事情，也可克制表演。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Under + play: turn down the “volume” of a presentation, whether minimizing an issue or acting with restraint.

etymology_story.zh: Banshee 来自爱尔兰语 bean sí，字面意为“仙丘之女”，其中 bean 表示“女人”，sí 与仙丘或仙界有关。在爱尔兰民间传说中，她的哭嚎被认为预示着某个家庭成员即将死亡。
etymology_story.en: Banshee comes from Irish bean sí, literally “woman of the fairy mound,” with bean meaning “woman” and sí referring to a fairy mound or the fairy world. In Irish folklore, her wailing was believed to foretell a death in a family.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 banshee 是不可再按英语词缀拆分的借词；bean + sí 属于其爱尔兰语来源结构。复数：banshees；透明派生形式：banshee-like／bansheelike（像报丧女妖的，尤指声音凄厉）；没有常用的独立动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, banshee is an unanalyzable borrowing; bean + sí belongs to its Irish source structure. Plural: banshees. Transparent derivative: banshee-like or bansheelike, especially describing a piercing cry. There are no common independent verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fairy（仙灵）是更宽泛的民俗类别，不一定报丧；wailing spirit（哀嚎的精灵）突出其声音，是描述性近义表达；harbinger of death（死亡的预兆或报信者）突出其预示死亡的作用，不限定为女性精灵。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fairy is a broader folklore category and need not announce death; wailing spirit is a descriptive near-equivalent emphasizing the sound; harbinger of death emphasizes the warning function without specifying a female spirit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “仙丘之女”开口哀嚎，传说中就是死亡将至的信号。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the “woman of the fairy mound”: her wail signals an approaching death.

senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员根据植物的生殖结构制定了一套分类方案。

etymology_story.zh: Classificatory 在英语中由 classification 所属词族的词干加形容词后缀 -ory 构成。其更早的来源包括拉丁语 classis，原指公民的等级或群体，后来“按共同特征分组”的意思扩展到了学术分类。
etymology_story.en: Classificatory was formed in English from the stem used in the classification word family and the adjective suffix -ory. Its deeper ancestry includes Latin classis, a division or class of citizens, whose grouping sense later extended to scholarly classification.

morphology_enriched.zh: classificat-（与 classification 共享的词干）+ -ory（具有……功能的；与……有关的）→ classificatory。主要词族：class（类别；分类）、classify（分类）、classification（分类；分类体系）、classifier（分类者；分类器）、classificatory（分类的）、classifiable（可分类的）、unclassifiable（无法分类的）、classified（已分类的；保密的）、unclassified（未分类的；非保密的）、misclassify（错误分类）、misclassification（错误分类）。
morphology_enriched.en: classificat- (the stem shared with classification) + -ory (serving a function; relating to) → classificatory. Main word family: class, classify, classification, classifier, classificatory, classifiable, unclassifiable, classified, unclassified, misclassify, and misclassification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: taxonomic（分类学的）通常涉及正式、系统的分类，尤常见于生物学；categorical（类别的）可强调类别划分，但也常表示“明确无疑的”，不能随意替换；classificational（分类的）语义接近，但较少见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Taxonomic usually concerns formal, systematic classification, especially in biology; categorical can concern categories but also commonly means unequivocal, so it is not freely interchangeable; classificational is close in meaning but less usual.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 class 就想到“类别”：classificatory 描述用来把事物归类的系统或方法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with class, meaning a group: classificatory describes the system or method used to put things into groups.

etymology_story.zh: Cravat 经法语 cravate 进入英语；该法语词源自当时对“克罗地亚人”的称呼。克罗地亚士兵佩戴的颈巾在法国引起注意后，族名逐渐变成了这种颈饰的名称。
etymology_story.en: Cravat entered English through French cravate, which came from a contemporary name for a Croat. After the neckcloths worn by Croatian soldiers attracted attention in France, the name of the people became the name of the accessory.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cravat 是整体借入的独立词干，不按英语词根和词缀拆分。复数：cravats；cravat + -ed → cravatted（戴领巾的），加后缀时末尾 t 双写；另有较少见的 uncravatted（未戴领巾的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cravat is a borrowed base rather than a combination of English roots and affixes. Plural: cravats. cravat + -ed → cravatted (wearing a cravat), with the final t doubled; the less common negative form is uncravatted.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 haberdassher 等形式指经营各类小商品的商人，更早的词源尚不确定。后来，英国英语主要保留了缝纫小用品商的含义，美国英语则发展出男装及配饰零售商的含义。
etymology_story.en: Middle English forms such as haberdassher referred to dealers in assorted small goods; the earlier origin is uncertain. British usage later specialized in sewing supplies, while American usage developed the meaning of a retailer of men's clothing and accessories.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 haberdasher 作为整体词干记忆，不宜因词尾形似 -er 就臆造独立词根。主要派生词：haberdasher + -y → haberdashery，表示相关商品、行业或店铺；复数为 haberdashers。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat haberdasher as a whole lexical base rather than inventing a separate root from its apparent -er ending. Its principal derivative is haberdasher + -y → haberdashery, meaning the goods, trade, or shop; the plural is haberdashers.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语 halcyon 追溯至希腊语 alkyōn，原指一种通常被认为是翠鸟的海鸟。古人相信它在冬季海面平静时筑巢，这一传说使鸟名逐渐获得“宁静美好的”这一形容词含义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Latin halcyon from Greek alkyōn, the name of a bird usually identified as a kingfisher. The ancient belief that it nested during calm winter weather at sea gave rise to the adjective meaning peaceful and happy.

morphology_enriched.zh: halcyon 在现代英语中是不可再作常用词缀分析的整体词干，同形用作形容词和名词。相关派生词有 halcyon + -ian → halcyonian（宁静美好的，罕见）；halcyon days 是固定搭配，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Halcyon is a whole lexical base in modern English, with the same form used as an adjective and a noun. A related derivative is halcyon + -ian → halcyonian, a rare adjective meaning peaceful or happy; halcyon days is a fixed expression rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peaceful（平静的）侧重没有冲突或干扰；idyllic（田园诗般美好的）强调近乎理想的幸福环境；carefree（无忧无虑的）强调没有烦恼。halcyon 尤常带有对昔日美好生活的怀念。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peaceful emphasizes freedom from conflict or disturbance; idyllic suggests an almost perfectly pleasant setting or life; carefree emphasizes freedom from worry. Halcyon especially evokes affectionate memories of a happier past.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 翠鸟筑巢，海浪平息：由平静海面联想到宁静美好的往日。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A nesting bird and a quiet sea: let the calm water suggest peaceful, happy days.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自晚期拉丁语 interrogativus，与拉丁语 interrogare“询问”同源；后者由 inter- 和 rogare“问、请求”构成。英语先将它用于提问和语法疑问形式，也用它描述带有询问意味的神情或语气。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Late Latin interrogativus, related to Latin interrogare, meaning to question, formed from inter- and rogare, to ask or request. English uses it both for grammatical question forms and for looks or tones that convey a question.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族可按 interrogate 去掉词尾 -e，再加 -ive → interrogative 理解；这是一种现代构词分析，实际词源为拉丁语借入。主要同族词包括 interrogate（询问、审问）、interrogation（询问、审问）、interrogator（审问者）、interrogatory（询问的；书面质询）、interrogatively（以疑问方式）和 non-interrogative（非疑问的）。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern word-family analysis, remove the final -e from interrogate and add -ive → interrogative; historically, the word was borrowed from Latin. Principal relatives include interrogate, interrogation, interrogator, interrogatory, interrogatively, and non-interrogative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: questioning（询问的）最接近日常神情或语气用法；inquiring（探询的）强调希望了解情况；inquisitive（好问的）强调求知欲，有时暗含爱打听。语法术语 interrogative 不能在所有场合用这些词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Questioning is the closest everyday equivalent for a look or tone; inquiring emphasizes seeking information; inquisitive emphasizes curiosity and can suggest excessive interest in others' affairs. These words do not replace interrogative in every grammatical context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: interrogate 是“发问”，interrogative 就是“起发问作用的”；作名词时指发问所用的词或结构。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Interrogate means to question; interrogative describes something that asks, or names the word or structure used to ask.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 Lyceum，源于希腊语 Lykeion，即雅典一处与阿波罗崇拜有关、亚里士多德曾在此讲学的场所。这个地名后来成为学校和公共讲学机构的名称，并用于十九世纪美国的公共讲学运动。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin Lyceum, from Greek Lykeion, an Athenian site associated with Apollo where Aristotle taught. The place-name later became a term for schools and public educational institutions, including those of the nineteenth-century American lyceum movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: lyceum 是整体借入的名词，现代英语中不宜强拆成有独立意义的常用词根与词缀。复数通常为 lyceums，也可用 lycea；常见复合表达包括 lyceum movement（公共讲学运动）和 lyceum lecture（公共教育讲座）。
morphology_enriched.en: Lyceum is a borrowed noun treated as a whole base in modern English, rather than split into productive roots and affixes. Its plural is usually lyceums, with lycea also available; common combinations include lyceum movement and lyceum lecture.
